- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.30) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to model output.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30), model underestimates; adjust downward by 5–10% to avoid missing upside momentum.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to avoid overshoots in the immediate future.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 2–5% to align with historical volatility patterns.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-stage trend continuation; increase final 5–7 days of forecast by 2–5% if sentiment remains positive.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a negative streak, model underreacts; add a 3–5% upward bias to forecast tail end.
- Avoid forecasting sharp downward moves unless sentiment is persistently negative (last 3 days < -0.30); model tends to underestimate downside risk in such cases.
